query: What is the current national norovirus category on the WastewaterSCAN dashboard as of today (High/Medium/Low), and is it rising, falling, or stable? Note the unusual summer 2026 GII.17 off-season surge.
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the summary:

**Current national norovirus category on WastewaterSCAN:** The last officially dated WastewaterSCAN nationwide figure (June 2026 newsletter, data through June 30, 2026) is **MEDIUM and FALLING** — median concentration down ~37% vs. May 2026, downward over the trailing 21 days, but still detected in 99% of samples. This reflected the normal post-winter-peak decline of the 2025–26 season.

**As of today (July 25, 2026):** WastewaterSCAN has **not yet published a July nationwide newsletter**, so MEDIUM/falling is the last confirmed category from its own reporting. A live dashboard check would be needed to confirm today's exact level.

**The summer 2026 GII.17 off-season surge:** Independent trackers and news coverage from early-to-mid July 2026 describe an unusual warm-season surge (atypical for summer), with ~12 states elevated — led by Utah, Texas, Ohio, and North Carolina — and wastewater anomalies preceding case surges in Utah and Texas. GII.17 rose from <10% of U.S. outbreaks in 2022–23 to ~75% in 2024–25 (CDC EID) via immune escape.

**Key caveat:** There's a data-vintage mismatch — the precise MEDIUM/falling reading is ~3–4 weeks old, and the June newsletter itself did not flag the summer/GII.17 surge; that narrative comes from other trackers. Sources also disagree on the current dominant strain (GII.17 vs. GII.4 Sydney), which is an unresolved uncertainty.
